question:
How should modules be organized so that the software stays easy to maintain, and how can an existing badly structured program be improved without its users noticing any difference?

Answer with a list of guidelines. After each guideline, cite the source it comes from: the path of the SWEBOK file if you have it, otherwise a verbatim quote of at least 8 words from the passage, in the form (source: ...).
answer:
# Summary

Good module organization requires applying principles like separation of concerns, encapsulation, high cohesion, and low coupling to keep software understandable and maintainable. Poorly structured programs can be improved through refactoring—reorganizing internals without changing external behavior—and reverse engineering to recover design understanding.

# Guidelines

- Organize modules so each has a single, well-defined responsibility, as smaller components with distinct functionalities are easier to understand and maintain. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Component Modularization and Single Responsibility Principle.md)

- Apply loose coupling between modules: [SWEBOK excerpt 8e09fd042699cb2e6740] to minimize interdependence. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md)

- Maximize cohesion within each module so its constituent elements are strongly related to one another. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md)

- Use encapsulation (information hiding) so [SWEBOK excerpt 59aee1f0a9b28a68eed9]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md)

- Separate interface from implementation: define a component by specifying its public interfaces and isolate [SWEBOK excerpt 9cb30d2095473b764f26]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md)

- Apply separation of concerns so each concern can be studied in isolation, enabling effective ordering of design thoughts. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture_ Foundations, Views, and Patterns/Defining Software Architecture and Its Scope/Stakeholders and Concerns in Software Systems.md)

- Decompose large software into smaller components or units through modularization, refinement, or decomposition. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Separation of Concerns and Modularization in Software Design.md)

- Design modules for modularity so [SWEBOK excerpt 3215940258d09bd2a584]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance Costs, Metrics, and Quality/Software Quality and Maintainability Metrics/Measurable Characteristics of Software Maintainability.md)

- Use refactoring [SWEBOK excerpt 9fbd812fb5aa3b52dd0c], improving internal structure and maintainability while keeping external behavior identical for users. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md)

- Apply continuous refactoring to reduce and manage [SWEBOK excerpt f1205b47bec9dec12a20]. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md)

- Use reverse engineering to analyze poorly structured software, identifying its components and interrelationships, and create representations at higher levels of abstraction to guide restructuring. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Refactoring and Reverse Engineering in Software Development.md)

- Record design rationale—including assumptions made, alternatives considered, and trade-offs analyzed—since reasons obvious to the current team may be unclear to those who later modify or maintain the system. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design Concerns, Documentation, and Modeling/Recording Design Rationale for System Maintainability.md)

- Address technical debt early: lack of modularity in an initial design can adversely affect development time for subsequent releases and compromise future maintainability, requiring extensive refactoring later. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture_ Foundations, Views, and Patterns/Architectural Design Languages, Decisions, and Technical Debt/Technical Debt and Software Architecture Process.md)

- [SWEBOK excerpt e51c8c330f014bb545ba] to avoid code clones and improve organization. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Construction Techniques and Practices/Software Reuse and Cloud-Based Development/Software Construction for and with Reuse.md)

- Apply uniformity—a principle of consistency across software components—so that common solutions are produced to address common or recurring problems. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Modular Design and Core Software Principles/Software Design Principles and Module Organization.md)

- During high-level design, define [SWEBOK excerpt ea0ae65a8a0d71da9403] in sufficient detail to allow client developers to access its capabilities without reading its code. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Foundations of Software Architecture/Software Architecture Foundations and Design Principles/Software Design Principles and Processes/Software Development Stages and Design Architecture/High-Level and Detailed Design Stages in Software Architecture.md)

- Use software visualization tools to [SWEBOK excerpt 9d9b5f9fd0b4b4b1c460], detect code smells, and estimate technical debt when improving existing programs. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Maintenance and Configuration Management/Software Maintenance, Evolution, and Quality Assurance/Software Visualization and Reverse Engineering Tools.md)

- Write [SWEBOK excerpt 7d6058e5a9e6b26a0e56], using modular design and coding standards to reduce complexity and ease maintenance. (source: /workspace/swebok-v4/root/Software Design and Construction Fundamentals/Software Construction and Code Complexity Management/Software Construction Tools and Anticipating Change.md)
